questions.q: Why were thirty thousand men and thousands of animals camped at Rawal Pindi?
choices: To be reviewed by the Viceroy of India
To wait for the rain to stop before marching
To guard the border against the Amir's army
To train new horses brought from Australia
questions.evidence: to be reviewed by the Viceroy of India

questions.q: What made the narrator's tent cave in and dance about "like a mad ghost"?
choices: A gust of wind snapped the pole
One of the Amir's wild horses kicked it
A camel blundered into it in the dark
Vixen the terrier tore the ropes loose
questions.evidence: A camel had blundered into it

questions.q: Where did the narrator finally make a place to rest for the night?
choices: Under a cart in the camel lines
In a friend's tent near the horse lines
Beside the guns in the artillery lines
Inside a stable with the battery mules
questions.evidence: I put my waterproof over the muzzle of one gun

questions.q: What are screw-guns, as the narrator explains them?
choices: Huge siege guns pulled across plains by bullocks
Small cannon in two pieces that mules carry up mountains
Rifles that the cavalry carry tied to their saddles
Guns fixed on the backs of elephants for battle
questions.evidence: tiny little cannon made in two pieces

questions.q: The camel says he fought "a white thing that waved" and it hit him with a stick. What was it really?
choices: A soldier in a white coat waving his rifle
A flag on a pole outside the officers' tents
The narrator's tent and its broken tent pole
A sheet hung out to dry on the cannon
questions.evidence: That was my broken tent pole

questions.q: What did Billy the mule do when he found out the camel had been disturbing the camp?
choices: He called the camel's driver to come and fetch him
He kicked the camel twice in the ribs
He chased the camel back to the camel lines
He told the camel to lie quietly beside the bullocks
questions.evidence: caught the camel two kicks in the ribs

questions.q: What reason did the baggage camel give for running all round the camp?
choices: He had dreamed bad dreams and was very afraid
The Amir's horses had broken into the camel lines
His driver had forgotten to tie his head-rope
He was looking for better grass to eat
questions.evidence: we dreamed bad dreams in the night, and we were very much afraid

questions.q: "'My lords,' said the camel humbly." How did the camel speak?
choices: Loudly and angrily, as if insulted
Meekly, as if he was less important
Proudly, as if boasting of his deeds
In a sleepy mumble, half awake

questions.q: How did the troop-horse try to make the frightened young mule feel better?
choices: He offered to stand guard while the mule slept
He told how he once ran for half a day after seeing a man
He said that camels were harmless and could not bite
He promised to find the young mule's driver for him soon
questions.evidence: I ran for half a day

questions.q: What did the gun-bullocks do when the camels came through their lines?
choices: They charged the camels and drove them away
They broke their chains and ran in a stampede
They got up and walked away once they were trampled
They bellowed until their drivers came to help
questions.evidence: when we were trampled on we got up and walked away

questions.q: According to the troop-horse, what is "the worst kind of cowardice"?
choices: Running away and leaving your rider behind
Being angry after you have been afraid
Pretending you were never scared at all
Telling scary stories to frighten others
questions.evidence: don't be angry after you've been afraid. That's the worst kind of cowardice

questions.q: What does the troop-horse mean when he says a horse must be "bridle-wise"?
choices: It knows how to slip out of its bridle at night
It spins round at once when the rein presses its neck
It stands still while the rider puts on the bridle
It can find its way home with no rider at all
questions.evidence: spin round at once when the rein is pressed on your neck

questions.q: How did Billy say battery mules are taught, compared with the horse?
choices: To obey the man who walks at their head
To kick at anyone carrying a knife
To spin around whenever they hear a gun
To follow the elephant wherever it goes
questions.evidence: We're taught to obey the man at our head

questions.q: What does the troop-horse believe matters most when he goes into battle?
choices: Being faster than all the other horses
Being able to see the enemy's knives
Trusting his own rider, Dick Cunliffe
Staying far back from the fighting
questions.evidence: If you don't trust your man, you may as well run away at once.

questions.q: What does Billy say is "the science of the thing" when climbing mountains with the guns?
choices: Always go straight up by the shortest path
Never let a man hold your head while climbing
Never show yourself against the sky line
Always carry the heaviest load at the front
questions.evidence: never to show up against the sky line

questions.q: How did the baggage camels fight in battle?
choices: They charged in a long line across the plain
They sat in a square while men fired over their backs
They carried the screw-guns up into the hills
They hid behind the elephants until the fighting was over

questions.q: Why do the gun-bullocks call "Two Tails" the elephant a great coward?
choices: He runs away whenever a camel comes near him
He will not go any nearer to the smoke of battle
He refuses to pull the guns across the rivers
He trumpets in fear at every little noise at night
questions.evidence: he is not going any nearer to the smoke

questions.q: What is this part of the story mostly about?
choices: Camp animals each describing their own way of serving in war
A camel learning to be brave from an old battery mule
Soldiers trying to catch the animals that ran loose at night
A troop-horse teaching the young mules to be bridle-wise
questions.evidence: That is the proper way to fight.
